To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CBDCA is encapsulated within the AFt nanocage and that the Pt centers coordinate to histidine residues on the inner surface.
the Pt centers of carboplatin are bound to the inner surface of apo ferritin nanocages, with two different binding sites.
the second-generation Pt anticarcinogen carboplatin (Pt(NH3)2Cl2) was encapsulated into apo-horse spleen ferritin and the X-ray crystal structure was determined to 1.49Å resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interactions between Pt drugs and the protein cage, which is a promising nanocarrier for the controlled delivery of anticancer drugs.
the synthesis of new Pt(II) and Pt(IV) compounds with potential anticancer activity, with the aim of improving the pharmacological and toxicological profile of the parent drug cisplatin.
the development of novel nanocarrier platforms for anticancer drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Pt centers of the CBDCA-loaded protein are located on the inner surface and that the Pt centers are not located at the same positions of the Pt centers of cisplatin- and cisplatin-loaded protein, which are located on the outer surface of the Ft cage.
CBDCA, in contrast to cisplatin, is able to form a Pt complex with the NE2 atom on the inner surface, but it cannot form a Pt complex in the central cavity of the Ft nanogage.
the Pt centers in CBDCA-encapsulated Ft bind to two different histidines on the protein inner surface and are not in contact with the Pt centers of the other Pt molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pt coordination geometry in CBDCA-encapsulated Ft is similar to that observed in cisplatin- or transplatin-encapped FT, with Pt coordinated to two histidine residues.
the Pt coordination environment is similar to that observed in cisplatin, but the Pt–Pt distances are significantly larger than those in the cisplatinum complex.
CBDCA, which has been extensively used in the clinic, is a suitable drug for the development of protein-based nanocarriers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CBDCA is able to bind to His residues that are not involved in the coordination of cisplatin, suggesting that the drug-loaded AFt may be useful for the delivery of CBDCA to cancer cells, where the drug can be released by the action of proteases and then bind to cellular targets.
the Pt centers of CBDCA are located on the inner surface, which suggests that the Pt centers may be accessible to the protein matrix and that the drug is likely to interact with protein residues.
Pt can be bound by the protein in different sites and that the Pt coordination environment can be different from that observed in cisplatin.
